practice.title: Glaciers and Rivers (≈ 190 palabras)
practice.passage:
Glaciers act as natural reservoirs, storing winter snow and releasing it gradually as meltwater during summer. For centuries, this rhythm has sustained rivers that millions of people depend on for drinking water and irrigation. As temperatures rise, however, the pattern is changing.

In the short term, accelerated melting actually increases river flow, which can create a false impression of abundance. Downstream communities may build new infrastructure on the assumption that the extra water will last. Yet once a glacier shrinks beyond a critical size, its contribution declines sharply, and rivers become more dependent on irregular rainfall.

The consequences vary by region. In humid mountain ranges, rainfall can partly compensate for lost meltwater. By contrast, in arid regions such as parts of Central Asia, summer flow relies almost entirely on ice, so its disappearance would be far more severe. Planners therefore emphasize the need to anticipate this "peak water" turning point rather than react after it passes.

options: A comparison of how different regions are affected
A definition followed by an example
items.explain: Contrasta cordilleras húmedas con regiones áridas (By contrast).
